title: Diffusion
examples: What is the concentration gradient in diffusion?
How does temperature affect the rate of diffusion?
Can you give an example of diffusion in plants?

explain.say: Diffusion is the movement of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration.
The concentration gradient is the difference in concentration between two areas.
Temperature is a factor; higher temperatures speed up the movement of particles.
Surface area is another factor; larger surfaces allow for more diffusion to happen.
The nature of the particle matters; some particles move through membranes more easily than others.
In real life, when you place food in water, the smell spreads out because of diffusion.

faq.a: It is simply the difference in the amount of particles between two places. You might also hear it called the concentration difference. Another way to ask is what drives the movement?
asks: What is the difference in concentration?

faq.q: Does temperature always increase the rate of diffusion?
faq.a: Generally, yes, because heat gives particles more energy to move faster. However, if the temperature gets too high, the particles can break down. You could also ask if there is an upper limit.
asks: What happens to diffusion at high heat?

faq.q: Does the size of the particle affect how fast it moves?
faq.a: Yes, smaller particles can move through spaces and membranes much more quickly. You might also ask if particle size is important for movement.
asks: Does size matter for diffusion rate?

faq.q: Is diffusion the same as active transport?
faq.a: No, diffusion is passive, meaning it needs no energy to move down the gradient. Active transport requires energy to move against the gradient. You could ask if energy is needed for diffusion.

faq.q: Does the surface area affect the rate of diffusion?
faq.a: Yes, a larger surface area gives more space for particles to move across. Think of it like having more windows in a room. You could ask if size matters for diffusion.
asks: Does bigger area mean faster diffusion?
How does surface size affect transport?

facts: Diffusion moves particles from an area of high concentration to low.
The concentration gradient is the driving force for diffusion.
Higher temperatures increase the kinetic energy and rate of diffusion.
Larger surface areas increase the rate of diffusion.
